name: Power Aware Dynamic Reallocation For Inference (RAPID)
problem: Disaggregated prefill/decode inference improves utilisation and throughput under fixed hardware capacity, but as model and cluster scales grow, power rather than compute becomes the dominant limiter of performance and cost efficiency.
mechanism: Joints GPU role assignment with power budgets, adding static and dynamic power reallocation on top of GPU reallocation, so that goodput is sustained under strict power caps rather than only under fixed hardware capacity.
speedup_reported: Up to 2x improvement in SLO attainment at peak load compared with a static assignment under the same power caps, 'without an increase in complexity or cost'. CAUTION: the abstract states no baseline cluster size, model, workload or cap value, so this is a directional claim of the authors' own and is weaker evidence than the measurement papers in this slice. The framing sentence - power rather than compute has become the dominant limiter - is the more durable contribution and is consistent with the rack-level power density figures recorded in supply/gb200-nvl72-rack-120kw-liquid-required.
notes: Included because it makes the power-as-binding-constraint argument explicitly in a serving-systems context, which is the datacenter-systems angle rather than the energy/carbon/algorithmic-efficiency line - it treats power as a schedulable resource binding SLO attainment, not as an environmental quantity. It should be read as corroboration of the constraint framing rather than as strong evidence for its own speedup number: a bare 2x with no baseline is exactly the kind of claim SCHEMA.md warns against, and it is recorded here with that caveat attached rather than dropped, because the constraint framing is the valuable part. Distinct from the other power-cap papers in this slice (Joule Point, Where Does the Energy Go, Characterizing Performance-Energy Trade-offs) in that it allocates power across heterogeneous GPU roles rather than tuning a cap on a homogeneous fleet.
